articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Dev Adds Option to Turn Off Controversial Scent Trails and More in New Update
articles.summary: Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles.
body: The Sony developer made good on its promise to investigate a proper on/off option when version 1.001.006 launched just hours ago. Its patch notes reveal more targeted changes as the studio works out the remaining kinks that have emerged in the days since Marvel's Wolverine launched for PlayStation 5.

There are three new toggle settings that players can now use to customize their gameplay experience: one for Whiskey Bottle scent trails, one for Material Crate Audio Clues, and one for Nightmare Door Roots. Those first two proved to be an especially hot topic online, with players criticizing in-game hints as one of a few examples of a game many feel is too 'hand-holdy.' Adding the option to completely turn these guides off should quiet those concerns, with a toggle for Nightmare Door Roots adding even more freedom for players to tailor their Marvel's Wolverine experience to their liking.

The new toggles are pretty straightforward. If players find the wavy visuals to be a bit too distracting, they can simply turn them off. As noted in the in-game settings, using Wolverine's Crate Finder and Whiskey Finder Adaptations will override any flipped toggles.
points: Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles.

articles.title: 11 anime to watch if you like Frieren
articles.summary: While Frieren remains singular, a handful of anime come close to capturing its laid-back atmosphere or exploring similar themes. Series like Delicious in Dungeon and The Apothecary Diaries aren’t direct analogues for Frieren, but they share its comforting spirit.
body: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End is unlike anything else. Madhouse’s anime adaptation of Kanehito Yamada’s manga has delivered two brilliant seasons, with a highly anticipated third season still to come. It’s difficult to fit Frieren neatly into a box: The series embraces shonen fantasy conventions, then subverts them in beautiful and moving ways. Its story considers the ephemeral nature of time, the depth of human connection, and the importance of savoring the journey itself. Although Frieren doesn’t shy away from action when the occasion demands it, the series is far more interested in quiet moments shaped by tranquility and nostalgia.
points: While Frieren remains singular, a handful of anime come close to capturing its laid-back atmosphere or exploring similar themes.

articles.title: Chris Hansen Announces His Own Documentary After Watching 'Fever Dream' Primetime and Grades Movie a D
articles.summary: Chris Hansen says he was more confused than offended by Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, and is answering this dramatized version of events with his own documentary. Chris Hansen has finally seen Primetime, which he watched in a Times Square theater alongside an audience of average moviegoers — and he…
body: He’s also got “a number of documentaries” about his life and career in the works, one of which is currently being shopped around to multiple different platforms.

Hansen delivered the news during an interview with fellow host and journalist Jesse Watters on his YouTube channel after watching Primetime, where he revealed the documentary’s title: I am Chris Hansen.

“It’s a project, a film, in which I cooperated, produced by folks obviously I know and work with, and it was in the works well before we even heard of Primetime,” he said. “It’s pretty good timing to have this thing out there with our agents shopping it on the West Coast to various platforms.”

Hansen went on to give his review of the movie, which he graded a D. (Hey, at least it wasn’t an F.) And while Hansen praised Robert Pattinson’s performance, he felt the actor’s portrayal of him deviated significantly from who he was as a person — to the point where it was like watching a totally different person on the screen. And that, for Hansen, makes it so separate from his own identity that it’s hard to be offended by it.

articles.title: Game Changer Fans Want More ‘Rulette,’ but Dropout CEO Sam Reich Isn't Convinced
articles.summary: First played in season 7 with Jeremy Culhane, Anna Garcia, and Oscar Montoya, “Rulette” is ripe for chaos. Players wear velcro suits that get dotted with random rules they receive after spinning a giant, The Price Is Right -style wheel.
body: Reich has seen the demand for a “Rulette” show, but he’s not necessarily sold on the idea. “I'm not convinced that ‘Rulette’ doesn't become repetitive once you've seen 10 episodes,” he says. “But, man, is it fun every time we do it.” He notes Josh Ruben’s “crashout” at the end of “Rulette 2” was one of his favorite moments from Season 8.

Reich and the Game Changer crew haven’t been shy about bringing back specific games, like “Sam Says.” “Make Some Noise” was also played a few times before being spun off into its own show. “Crowd Control” didn’t even have the chance to return as a game samer; its spinoff show was filmed before the Game Changer episode even aired.
When contemplating what games should return, Reich and his fellow producers have several questions they need to answer when examining the games.

“Most importantly, is this scalable? Is it still exciting after you've seen seven episodes of it?” Reich explains. “And that could do with the Game Changer episode's popularity, but it could also do with, how different would these episodes be from each other? Or how repetitive?”

articles.title: How to Play the Silent Hill Games in Order
articles.summary: Silent Hill has appeared in the restless dreams of horror fans for almost three decades now. The foggy town and its various iterations, plagued by the Otherworld, continue to define the mechanics and ambience of psychological horror to this day.
body: Each Silent Hill game contains a relatively standalone story, tied to whatever character the Otherworld has decided to bring to its doorstep. However, the lore of Silent Hill develops across games through returning characters as well as memos, posters, and other small details. Despite its fill of contradictions, some of which are only natural for games with multiple endings, there’s a larger story lurking in the background of each protagonist’s path to atonement (or madness).
If the release of Silent Hill: Townfall has sparked your curiosity about how the timeline all fits together, we’ve got you covered.
Approximately 18 Silent Hill games have been released since the franchise debuted in 1999.

Four Silent Hill games were originally developed by Team Silent between 1999 and 2004. Subsequent games, including plenty of spinoffs, were developed by a variety of studios across Japan and North America.

articles.title: CBS's Legendary 156-Episode Sci-Fi Anthology Series is Officially Free to Watch on Streaming
articles.summary: In the realm of science fiction, pretty much all roads lead to, or derive from, The Twilight Zone. And this landmark show is currently free to stream on Tubi.
body: In the realm of science fiction, Star Wars and Star Trek are generally considered to be the two biggest franchises. And, if you’re purely talking about profitability, that’s correct, as those two have dominated TV and film for decades. However, if you factor in things like influence and impact, another sci-fi property ranks up there with the big two.

Debuting in 1959, The Twilight Zone ran for five seasons on CBS, totaling 156 episodes. It was created by Rod Serling, a television pioneer who sought to expand what had been seen on television throughout the 1950s, much of which was taped plays and multi-camera sitcoms like I Love Lucy. To do this, he created The Twilight Zone, a single-camera anthology series where each episode would operate like a little movie (for most of its run, the show ran for a half-hour, but season 4 tried out an hour-long format before switching back to half-hours for season 5).
points: In the realm of science fiction, pretty much all roads lead to, or derive from, The Twilight Zone.

articles.title: Ridley Scott's Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Masterpiece is Officially Streaming on YouTube for Free
articles.summary: By the ‘80s, that pessimism curdled into a fully realized vision, and no film played a larger role in that than Scott’s Blade Runner. Its production is also one of the most infamous studio-creator struggles in Hollywood, with five different cuts released over the years.
body: The ‘70s and ‘80s were a major turning point for science fiction. Star Wars revitalized the genre and turned it into one of Hollywood’s main box office draws, inspiring a wave of films that are still shaping sci-fi today. Then, in the late ‘70s, Ridley Scott threw down the gauntlet with Alien, taking a clear step away from the optimism that had once permeated these stories and instead infusing it with corporate anxiety and untrustworthy artificial intelligence. It was a signal for things to come.

Blade Runner begins with an opening crawl, throwing you into a corporate world where bioengineered humanoids called replicants exist. These androids have rapidly advanced, with each generation boasting skills that go beyond human abilities. They're stronger, smarter, faster, and more agile than us. After being treated as slaves for years, the replicants revolted, resulting in the formation of a police unit called Blade Runners tasked with retiring them. The replicants were ultimately outlawed on Earth. “Los Angeles, November, 2019,” reads the film’s sober title card, cutting to an establishing shot of the city at night, drowned by pollution, with giant buildings spewing fire.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Attempts To Kill Remaining Xbox Goodwill
articles.summary: After Xbox laid off 1,600 employees over the summer, Microsoft's gaming division followed up with more layoffs and studio closures this week. In the wake of these events, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is taking a look at the bright side and praising Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's actions as a necessary step.
body: "There's some amount of streamlining the team is doing, and Asha is doing, which is great to see," said Nadella during his appearance on the Sources Podcast. He also noted that he feels "fantastic about the IP we have right now. If I look at the studios, the IP portfolio we have, and our ability to then take that and produce great games going forward, I feel fantastic."
"We have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people," added Nadella.
Regarding AI, Nadella questioned why Western consumers are so skeptical about the technology compared to other parts of the world.

Prominent AI skeptic Ed Zitron has blamed Xbox's precarious position on " catastrophic mismanagement " by Microsoft and AI bets that didn't pan out. Even after the most recent layoffs, there are indications that more job cuts are coming to Xbox.

articles.title: Infinity Festival Returns to Los Angeles in November With a Focus on AI
articles.summary: Infinity Festival, an annual event celebrating the convergence of entertainment, technology, and creativity, is returning to Los Angeles this November for its 9th edition.
body: In previous years, the festival has hosted guests like Avengers directors the Russo Brothers, Brie Larson, Jon Favreau, Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, Jeff Bridges, and many more. This year, the festival promises to dive deep into AI, with panels focusing on its “growing role across the creative industries.” Instead of a standalone track, AI will be present through a broader program “spanning animation, gaming, sports tech, filmmaking, music, virtual production, and live entertainment.”

At the event, AI-focused programming will “explore the evolving tools and workflows behind animation and filmmaking, the growing crossover between gaming and entertainment, new technologies reshaping live sports and fan experiences, as well as advances in immersive production and live event design.”

Additionally, longtime partners like NVIDIA and HP will participate in the festival’s 2026 programming slate, which will feature “panels, keynotes, screenings, demonstrations, and exhibitions, with speakers and programming to be announced in the coming weeks.”

articles.title: This Diablo 4 Trick Lets You Become Stronger Than Ever, But It Might Not Be Intended
articles.summary: Diablo 4 players are decking themselves out in full sets of Mythic Unique gear as part of Season 15, resulting in characters that are more powerful than ever before. Whether that was Blizzard's goal, or this is simply a mistake of some kind, is currently up for debate.
body: It's about as big of a change from one season to the next that Diablo 4 has ever experienced. Back in Season 14, Blizzard added the "crafted" item tag to Mythic Uniques made via the Horadric Cube, Blacksmith, or Jeweler, with a limit of only one crafted Mythic being equippable at a time. Even if you had the Resplendent Sparks resource needed to make more Mythics, you couldn't use them. Instead, you had to rely on good old-fashioned luck to find natural Mythic drops without the crafted tag.

The changes weren't popular, so Blizzard walked it back mid-season, and has made further improvements as part of the latest season, Hell's Legacy. Mythics made by the Blacksmith or Jeweler are no longer considered "crafted," while ones made via the cube still are. Once again, players could have several Mythics of your own creation equipped at once, much like the previous seasons.
However, for players with more sparks than they know what to do with, there is technically a way to get around the "crafted" tag.
points: Diablo 4 players are decking themselves out in full sets of Mythic Unique gear as part of Season 15, resulting in characters that are more powerful than ever before.

articles.title: Yes, Beyond Good & Evil 2 Is Somehow Still In Development
articles.summary: No news is good news, they say. They also say that some news, however little, is good news, too, and girl, do we have some news: Ubisoft's struggling action-adventure game Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still alive despite remaining in development hell.
body: Ubisoft Bordeaux's lead writer and associate narrative director Rik Godwin took to Bluesky on September 22 to provide a brief update on the game.

"Odd sort of non-announcement but for the past few months I've been working on Beyond Good & Evil 2 in a support/consultant role," Godwin, who was a writer on Assassin's Creed Shadows, said. "I am allowed to say this, I checked."

It makes sense that Ubisoft Bordeaux would assist with Beyond Good & Evil 2. According to IGN, Ubisoft Montpellier, which is leading the project's development, is just south of the Bordeaux studio. And although Ubisoft Bordeaux was the lead developer on both 2023's Assassin's Creed Mirage and Shadows' 2025 expansion Claws of Awaji, that studio typically operates in a support role for Ubisoft's myriad other teams.

articles.title: Drop everything and grab the popcorn: Majuular's 4.5-hour documentary on Ultima Online is here to devour your weekend
articles.summary: I'll make this quick: Whatever you had planned for the weekend, you've got to carve four-and-a-half hours out for a last-minute swerve into the late '90s. Six months in the making, YouTube essayist Majuular is back with the (I believe) penultimate video in his multi-year Ultima series.
body: "From its unlikely formation at the behest of Richard Garriott and Starr Long, to its tempering at the hands of Raph Koster and his team of Multi-User Dungeon enthusiasts, to its changing identity in the face of competition, to its incalculable influence, this is the story of Ultima Online," the description reads. If you get the Ultima Online bug after watching the documentary, good news: it's still very much playable on both official servers and fan ones. Majuular highlighted the server he played on, In Mani Ylem, which aims to recapture the late '90s experience.

You can find the entire video series in a playlist here, and I can't recommend watching them highly enough. In late 2025 we published a feature story about Majuular's quest to chronicle the making of Richard Garriott's genre-defining series, and how that mission unexpectedly catapulted him to YouTube success with more than 200,000 followers. It's a good read—and won't take you quite as long as watching all the videos.

articles.title: Switch Pirate Ignored Nintendo’s Lawsuit, Now He Owes $4.5 Million
articles.summary: After suing a former Reddit moderator in October 2025 for pirating Switch games, a Washington court has ordered the individual in question to pay Nintendo $4.5 million in damages.
body: According to a September 25 TorrentFreak report, US District Judge Lauren King ordered former r/SwitchPirates moderator James "Archbox" Williams to cough up $4.5 million in damages to Nintendo after the company accused him of operating several pirate shops to illegally decrypt and distribute Switch games to the public.

The lawsuit, which was filed in a Washington federal court in June 2024, stated that Williams had been running this racket since at least 2019, using "circumvention device" software to bypass the company's systems and gain access to over 30 Nintendo Switch games. This includes titles like The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Williams reportedly ignored the complaint at the time, which prompted Nintendo to seek the statutory maximum of $150,000 per title in October 2025. And just this week, Judge King agreed with Nintendo's request, stating that Williams was aware of the case, as he both hired a lawyer to object to a Google subpoena and continued posting on Reddit but opted to not respond to the company's lawsuit.
points: After suing a former Reddit moderator in October 2025 for pirating Switch games, a Washington court has ordered the individual in question to pay Nintendo $4.5 million in damages.

videos.title: Ariadne's Tale - Announcement Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Step into Ariadne's Tale, a first-person puzzle adventure that reinvents the classic myth with wit and dark humour. As Ariadne, you carry a magical thread that guides your path and serves as a tool to fix routes, anchor points and activate mechanisms.
body: Each chamber is a test of observation and creativity: combine puzzle solving, object manipulation and lateral thinking to progress. The narrative blends ironic voices with a mythic atmosphere: an architect guides (and nags) you through a magical conch, while the terror and beauty of the Labyrinth slowly unfold. The goal is clear: find and rescue Theseus… before the threads of fate are cut.
points: Step into Ariadne's Tale, a first-person puzzle adventure that reinvents the classic myth with wit and dark humour.
As Ariadne, you carry a magical thread that guides your path and serves as a tool to fix routes, anchor points and activate mechanisms.
Use the thread to orient yourself, manipulate devices and reach the heart of the Labyrinth before the beast finds you.
Each chamber is a test of observation and creativity: combine puzzle solving, object manipulation and lateral thinking to progress.
